Residual gap: a turn that stops and then fails (answer validation, cancel, session liveness check, completion error) leaves no trace of the stop, because those paths write fixed messages without metadata. Acceptable only if the answer-only sink is accepted.

signature_hash is an unkeyed blake3 digest of the tool name and canonical arguments. For low-entropy arguments (a bare URL or a short query) a stored hash can be confirmed by guessing, so it is not strictly content-free on persistent and waived turns. ZDR turns never reach the tool loop. Decide before any enforce flip: keep it, switch to a per-process keyed hash, or drop it and keep tool, reason and count.

Waived turns (zdr_waived) persist their answer message like persistent turns, so the entry is written there too. It is content-free, but DEC-32 says waived runs count as ZDR for new durable stores. The owner should confirm reuse of the answer metadata for waived turns.

The wiring from ToolRounds.loop_stop to the persisted answer is pinned by source text, and the helper by unit tests. No behavioural test drives an enforced stop through invoke_stream_sse to the stored message. That needs the inference-stub harness, the same gap as the earlier round.

The row says loop_stop is saved content-free in run/step audit detail. The code instead writes it into the streaming answer message's metadata Struct (sse.rs with_loop_stop wrapping stamp_generation). The lead must accept this sink or move it before enforce is switched on.

A turn that stops under enforce and then fails afterwards (validation, cancel, liveness or completion error) writes a fixed message with no metadata. The stop then leaves only a log line and a metric, with no durable trace.

signature_hash is an unkeyed blake3 hash of the tool name plus the canonical arguments. It is persisted in answer metadata and logged at info level, so a low-entropy argument such as a URL or a short query can be confirmed by guessing. Decide between a keyed hash, a truncated hash or dropping it before enforce.

Waived (DEC-32) turns persist their answer, so loop_stop lands in their metadata as well. ZDR turns cannot write it, because sse.rs returns at the effective_zdr branch (~1701) before any tool loop. The owner should confirm reuse of the answer metadata for waived turns.

depth_findings.text: The RUN_ATTENTION notifier has no still-requested re-check, so an approval decided after its event was written, or one past its sweep window, still notifies the user; the W2-29 ledger entry lists this as open before the switch goes on, and it needs a session-core read over the API, not a database read across planes.

The channel-aware gate covers only the three attention types: the design says it fixes the per-type gate for all types, but changing legacy types while every switch is off breaks the owner's byte-identical rule for users with partial preference rows, so the owner must choose between a default-off switch for the legacy types and accepting that change.

For the native types an email or push opt-out does not suppress anything and an in-app opt-out suppresses the request, so a user who wants only email gets no attention request at all, because native delivery is their only deliverer in this build; the email path belongs with S6 and needs an owner decision.

Turning CAPABILITY_CORE_ATTENTION_NOTIFY_ENABLED on before NOTIFICATION_NATIVE_TYPES_ENABLED makes every attention request fail at the disabled provider with 502; capability-core Naks every non-2xx, so JetStream redelivers until MaxDeliver, and the MaxDeliver of capability-core-run-watch-notify has to be read before the switch goes on.

The definition of done is not proved: rebuild notification-core and capability-core, record NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_MODE and the native switch, then run a gated approval with the tab closed and check one notification_feed_items row of type modelplane.needs_approval, the BFF notifications read, the email-off case still showing in-app, and a watched run_completed still notifying.
The coalescing window lives in each capability-core process, so N replicas can send up to N notifications in one window; a durable window needs a store that this slice does not own.

The idempotency key attention:{org}:{run}:{user}:{state}:{source} can exceed notification-core's 256-byte limit when ids are long, and the resulting validation error would be Nak'd forever; hash the key or check id lengths before the switch goes on.
No migration contract asserts migration 015's rows (three types, in_app and push on, email off); the pattern is internal/database/delivery_migration_contract_test.go, which this slice does not own.

The cross-service coupling is pinned only by literals: capability-core's state-to-type map and notification-core's native closed key set have no shared golden, only NEEDS_APPROVAL crosses the run-attention golden, and nothing is mutation-tested, which the Model Plane CLAUDE.md asks for on cross-service coupling.

notification-core accepts the three attention types from capability-core whenever they arrive, because isNotificationTypeAuthorized is not gated by NOTIFICATION_NATIVE_TYPES_ENABLED; capability-core emits them only behind its own switch, so gating the allowlist on the native switch is an owner choice.
The snake_case reconcile of notifications-client.ts and the message_key localisation are not done; the row ties them to WS01-S0, and the live tree carries the cta_href and event_type drift.

The process IsZDR ack now applies to run_completed and run_failed; grep found no producer that sets zdr:true on those subjects (learning events are withheld for ZDR runs and the Go orchestrator never sets Zdr), so nothing changes observably today, but any future producer that sets it is silently dropped, by design.

A ledger entry for WS16-D2 and DEC-38 belongs in apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md (native adapter for allowlisted content-free types, the in-app-only gate, the all-types gate deferred); this slice does not own that file.
The notification-core README paragraph describes the in-app-only gate; update it once the owner decides the two gate questions above.

The row asks for a channel-aware gate `EnabledChannels` (suppressed only when every channel is off) that fixes the per-type bug for all types, but the build applies an in-app-only gate to the three native types and leaves legacy types on IsNotificationEnabled (service.go isNotificationEnabled). The deviation is defensible under the switches-off byte-identical rule, but the owner must pick: fix the legacy types behind a flag, or accept the change unflagged.

processAttention (runwatch/attention.go) has no still-requested re-check, so an approval decided after session-core wrote its RUN_ATTENTION event still notifies the user. W2-29 lists this re-check as a precondition for switching the path on, and it needs a session-core API read, not a database read across planes.

If CAPABILITY_CORE_ATTENTION_NOTIFY_ENABLED goes on while NOTIFICATION_NATIVE_TYPES_ENABLED is off, the attention types are accepted (the allowlist is not gated) and sent to the disabled Novu provider. The provider fails them, and capability-core Naks every non-2xx, so JetStream redelivers until MaxDeliver. Enforce the switch order, or gate the allowlist entries on the native switch.

The idempotency key attention:{org}:{run}:{user}:{state}:{source} has no length check against notification-core's 256-byte limit. With long ids the request fails validation, and processAttention would Nak it on every redelivery; hash the key or bound the id lengths.
The coalescing window is in-process (attentionNotify.lastSent), so N capability-core replicas can each notify once per window.

isNotificationEnabled takes the in-app-only native branch for the three types even when WithNativeDelivery is off. In that configuration the provider path runs under a different gate than legacy types, a mixed mode no test pins beyond TestNativeTypeWithoutNativeDeliveryKeepsTheProviderPath.
No migration contract test asserts the rows of migration 015 (three types, in_app and push on, email off); the pattern is internal/database/delivery_migration_contract_test.go.

capability-core's state-to-type map and notification-core's nativeTypes/nativePayloadKeys sets are coupled only by duplicated literals, with no shared golden and no mutation test. Only NEEDS_APPROVAL is covered by the run-attention golden.
The IsZDR() ack in process now also covers run_completed/run_failed envelopes with zdr:true. No producer sets that today, so nothing changes observably; the row asks for this behaviour.
The README paragraph on the in-app-only gate needs an update once the owner settles the gate decisions above.
